cases.label: sc_compose_cli_only
cases.strategy: Direct `sc-compose render --mode file` against a fixed temp-root template and JSON var-file. No sc-cron, no Monty, no Python—baseline for what a host bridge should call.

cases.label: python_render_only
cases.strategy: Fresh `python3 -c` each tick: import PyO3 `sc_compose`, call `render_template(str, dict)`. Models per-tick cold subprocess + interpreter startup (worst case for compose in Python).

cases.label: cpython_hook (PythonHook::invoke)
cases.strategy: Full sc-cron path: `PythonHook` spawns `python3 <fixture>` with `cron.tick`, hook JSON on stdin; fixture calls `sc_compose.render_template` from payload. Production `HookTarget::Python` pattern (isolated child + timeout/kill).

cases.in_process_rss_note: getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF) high-water after timed loop (includes cargo test + Monty VM; not an isolated Monty-only process)
cases.label: monty_host_bridge + sc-compose CLI
cases.strategy: Lab only (not production sc-cron yet): `MontyRepl::feed_start` runs snippet `render_template(...)`; host registers ext fn `render_template`, resumes with output from Rust `sc-compose` CLI (same temp-root files). Hook logic stays in Monty; compose stays out of CPython.

cases.in_process_rss_note: getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF) high-water after timed loop (includes cargo test + Monty VM; not an isolated Monty-only process)
cases.label: production monty_host bridge
cases.strategy: Production path: `HookTarget::Monty` schedule row, `Scheduler::run_due`, `drive_feed` → `execute_feed_with_compose_program` resumes `render_template` and spawns `sc-compose` (no lab `feed_start` in this harness).
